paper_title: Constraining Rapidly Oscillating Scalar Dark Matter Using Dynamic Decoupling
suggested_experiment_name: Dynamic Decoupling Sr+ ion clock vs optical cavity (Weizmann DD scalar DM search)
coupling_convention: g_phi-gamma in eV^-1 as plotted on Fig. 2b y-axis (linear-in-phi scalar-photon coupling; NOT converted to dimensionless d_e)
notes: Paper presents a new, measured 95% CL exclusion limit on scalar DM couplings g_phi-gamma (photon, i.e. alpha variation) and g_phi-e (electron mass variation) using dynamic decoupling on a single 88Sr+ ion clock transition vs. cavity-stabilized laser, over frequencies ~Hz-MHz (masses ~4e-15 to ~4e-9 eV; best sensitivity at nu_m=1013 Hz, m~4.2e-12 eV). Coupling type is primarily ScalarPhoton (d_alpha sensitivity over the full range; m_e sensitivity only above ~50 kHz), consistent with pre-analysis hint. However, all numerical limits are presented only in figures (Figs. 1, 2a-c, 3) with no tables or explicit numerical values in the text; the y-axis values cannot be reliably read from the text-extracted content, so no data points are extracted. Assumed local DM density rho = 3.1e-6 eV^4 = ~0.4 GeV/cm^3 (Salucci et al.). Paper also gives projections (dashed lines) and relaxion mixing-angle bounds; note g_phi-gamma is quoted in eV^-1 in the paper.
